reason: The core drill is the direct way to sample ice from the sheltered band, as it was at the reference site.
expectation: The drill should retrieve a sealed core from within the band for the refrigerated case.

effect: The sealed core preserves the brown band between layers of clear ice; it now needs refrigerated transport.
reaction: The intact layers make the sample more informative than loose material.
reason: The buffered field case has a refrigerated cradle intended for this core.
expectation: The sealed core should be secured in the refrigerated case for the return trip.

effect: The core reached the laboratory frozen in its original liner, preserving the brown band and surrounding ice; the chapter goal is complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to bring back a sample with its geological context intact.

mostWorthwhile.text: Taking the interior core was most worthwhile: the clear ice above and below the brown band gave the sample context and made the scientific purpose tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Securing the core in the case was a predictable follow-up, though its refrigeration and safe return had a clear purpose.

surprise.text: The core preserved clear ice on both sides of the brown band, making the layer's surroundings visible rather than collecting brown material alone.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary; drilling the protected interior and refrigerating the sealed core both followed from the sampling goal.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to learn what examination of the preserved band reveals, although this short chapter offered few decisions beyond the obvious sampling sequence.
